dimensions.assessment: Affects federal agencies, state agencies, and deceased individuals' estates or beneficiaries by preventing improper benefit payments.
dimensions.evidence: The Commissioner of Social Security shall, to the extent feasible, provide information furnished to the Commissioner... to the agency operating the Do Not Pay working system...

dimensions.assessment: Improves administrative coordination for federal and state payments and requires clear and convincing evidence before recording a death.
dimensions.evidence: The Commissioner of Social Security may not record a death to a record... unless the Commissioner of Social Security has found it has clear and convincing evidence...

dimensions.assessment: Aims to reduce and recover improper federal and state payments, though specific dollar savings are not quantified in the source.
dimensions.evidence: ...to help prevent improper payments of, and support the recovery of improperly paid, benefits or other payments...

dimensions.assessment: Amends the Social Security Act to make data-sharing permanent, adds evidentiary thresholds for death records, and mandates error notifications.
dimensions.evidence: Section 205(r) of the Social Security Act... is amended by striking paragraph (11) and inserting the following...

dimensions.assessment: Permanent statutory amendment taking effect December 27, 2026.
dimensions.evidence: The amendments made by this section shall take effect on December 27, 2026.

missing_information: Exact monetary estimates of improper payments prevented or recovered.
importance_detail.rationale: Permanently allows the Department of the Treasury's Do Not Pay system to access SSA death records to prevent improper payments, while instituting evidentiary standards and error-notification requirements.

card.label: S. 269
card.summary: The Ending Improper Payments to Deceased People Act makes permanent the requirement that the Social Security Administration share its death records with the Treasury Department's Do Not Pay system. It also requires the Social Security Administration to have clear and convincing evidence before recording an individual as deceased, and allows the agency to notify relevant government entities if someone is incorrectly marked as dead.
